name: Killdozer
label: Touch and Go
lede: Three Madison guys took their name from a TV movie about a possessed bulldozer, dedicated an EP to a folk singer who was still alive, handed Butch Vig the record that got him the Nirvana job, and signed off on a tour called Fuck You, We Quit!

eras.title: Basements, beer and cigars
eras.text: Killdozer played slow on purpose and sang about the people around them in Madison, Wisconsin: bikers without bikes, hoarders, drunks, Ed Gein. They recorded at a small studio run by Butch Vig and Steve Marker, years before Vig was famous.

years.big: "I cultivated my voice with beer and cigars."
years.h: Three Madison friends name a band after a TV bulldozer
years.p: [[Michael Gerald|bedbb6eb-bd46-4643-819f-8db9ef6564c9]] on bass and vocals, Bill Hobson on guitar and his brother Dan Hobson on drums borrow the title of Killdozer!, a 1974 TV movie about a possessed bulldozer. That's Gerald on where the growl came from.
years.xp:
The basement shows in Madison came before the name did. Bill Hobson told Isthmus he and Gerald "really hated that fast sound," so they played as slowly as they could.

Gerald's growl began as a rehearsal joke, and the Hobsons insisted he use it on everything. [[Butch Vig|ba30915c-4d33-43c5-8c37-ead0b8061517]] talked him out of trying to sing straight. The songs, Gerald said, were meant to make his friends laugh.

years.src: Wikipedia: Intellectuals Are the Shoeshine Boys of the Ruling Elite
years.h: Intellectuals Are the Shoeshine Boys of the Ruling Elite
years.p: Recorded in November 1983 at Smart Studio in Madison with Steve Marker and Vig, the debut came out on Bone Air Records. Touch and Go reissued it in 1989.
years.xp: The only cover is Creedence Clearwater Revival's Run Through the Jungle. Maximumrocknroll heard jazzy-metal playing, extremely gruff vocals and smart-ass lyrics.
play: Intellectuals Are the Shoeshine Boys of the Ruling Elite

years.h: Snakeboy is the first Killdozer album on Touch and Go
years.p: Recorded in March 1985 at Smart Studio with Marker, Vig and Duke Erikson. Much of it is about Gerald's encounter with a man named Bill Reisman.
years.xp: The only cover is Neil Young's Cinnamon Girl, and Jessica Noll plays violin on River. Vig remixed King of Sex for a 2006 tribute album.

eras.title: Burl Ives wasn't dead yet
eras.text: Killdozer kept its day jobs and put out a record nearly every year: a memorial EP for a man who was still alive, a covers album that crawled through American Pie, and the one that got Vig the call that changed his life.

years.h: Burl is dedicated to Burl Ives, who was still alive
years.p: The EP's dedication remembers the folk singer as if he'd died; he lived until 1995. The Wisconsin Boys Choir sings backup on the Jessi Colter cover I'm Not Lisa.
years.xp: It was recorded at Multi-Trac in Detroit, with Touch and Go's [[Corey Rusk|7e85d4b9-f01b-4d5f-892b-523daae2917c]] and Vig producing. Vig told Isthmus that people kept trying to break into the place, and Rusk stood outside with a cattle prod.

years.src: Wikipedia: Little Baby Buntin' · The Vinyl District
years.h: A Madison biker gang with no bikes gets a song
years.p: Little Baby Buntin', the third album, includes The Puppy, which Gerald based on Satan's Dragons, a Madison gang whose members didn't own motorcycles. There's also a Neil Diamond cover.
years.xp: Gerald said the song grew out of a real initiation that went horribly wrong. The Vinyl District's obituary of the band calls Killdozer the greatest protest band ever.

yt: American Pie live at Club X, 1989
years.h: Nine covers, and an 8:45 American Pie
years.p: The all-covers For Ladies Only, cut at Smart Studio with Vig, drags Don McLean's American Pie, Arthur Alexander's Burnin' Love and the Steve Miller Band's Take the Money and Run through the sludge.
years.xp: Besides LP, CD and a picture disc, it came as a box of five colored 7" singles with a bonus cover of Neil Young's Mr. Soul. NME gave it 9 out of 10.

years.h: Twelve Point Buck gets Vig the Nirvana job
years.p: Sub Pop's Jonathan Poneman heard it and sent [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]] to Vig to record demos. Kurt Cobain later wanted Nevermind to hit as heavy.
years.xp:
Vig told Isthmus the record opened a lot of doors, and that Poneman wanted "that attitude" for Nirvana. He described the Killdozer sound as a push and pull, like being seasick. The album reached No. 16 on the UK indie chart, and the Washington Post called its thump-and-grind art music.

Wikipedia says the album also brought Vig to [[Billy Corgan|3cbfd3e3-6d9b-4327-84ba-42cf646c98f9]]'s attention before [[The Smashing Pumpkins|ba0d6274-db14-4ef5-b28d-657ebde1a396]]' Gish.

years.h: Bill Hobson quits Killdozer, twice, and the band stops
years.p: He leaves before a European tour and [[Tom Hazelmyer|d6569a63-5da9-41fa-a5c9-b6b11b496218]] of [[Halo of Flies|3a26de45-4f41-4e28-bdc8-fda60ef0c8d0]], who runs AmRep, fills in. Hobson returns, then walks out during a recording session, AllMusic says.
years.xp: Killdozer went quiet after that. Gerald's tour diary from the period ran in Your Flesh in winter 1990, with notes on cold Iowa, Old Style half-barrels and the joy of a day that starts at Waffle House.

eras.title: Trotskyites with a bulldozer
eras.text: Michael Gerald and Dan Hobson came back with a new guitarist and album titles that sounded like Marxist slogans. Steve Albini recorded the last one, and by the end Gerald was the only founder left.

yt: Unbelievable live at Club D, Madison, 1992
years.h: Paul Zagoras joins on guitar and Killdozer is back
years.p: Gerald and Dan Hobson restart the band and release the single The Pig Was Cool.

years.h: A comeback album titled like a pamphlet
years.p: Uncompromising War on Art Under the Dictatorship of the Proletariat is the return record. Gerald called himself a Trotskyite, The Vinyl District reported.
years.xp: The CD adds the whole Burl EP, with liner notes admitting Burl Ives hadn't died yet and might still be alive.

years.src: Wikipedia: God Hears Pleas of the Innocent
years.h: Albini records God Hears Pleas of the Innocent
years.p: The last studio album was cut in September 1994 at the House That Dripped Blood in Chicago. The only cover is Lee Hazlewood's Pour Man.
years.xp: The Washington Post heard an alternate universe where Black Sabbath taught Robert Johnson the blues. The Chicago Tribune called it uproariously brutish, heavy and slow.
play: God Hears Pleas of the Innocent

yt: Interview and live, Victoria BC, September 1995
years.h: Drummer Dan Hobson leaves for his family
years.p: AllMusic says he steps away from Killdozer to focus on family. Erik Tunison of [[Die Kreuzen|7550b236-f9c2-450c-81a6-fac63bf9d23e]] takes the drums, and Jeff Ditzenberger of Power Wagon joins on second guitar.

years.src: Rebel Noise · Chicago Reader · Wikipedia: Killdozer
years.h: Gerald ends Killdozer with the Fuck You, We Quit! tour
years.p: Michael Gerald, the last founder standing, told the Chicago Reader why it ended. The farewell tour carried the title Fuck You, We Quit!
years.xp:
In the Reader's words, the split was "an inability to continue touring." Gerald said at the time he wanted to pursue other interests, and recalled that some longtime fans at the last shows needed babysitters to get there.

The same year Killdozer shared a split, Michael Gerald's Party Machine Presents!, with Alice Donut, a band Gerald had met at a Berlin disco.

eras.title: Fuck You, We Reunite!
eras.text: After the farewell the founders scattered into tax law, film crews and nursing. Touch and Go's 25th birthday brought the original trio back, on one rule: the band could never get in the way of the day jobs.

years.h: The Last Waltz captures the farewell live
years.p: Man's Ruin Records puts out a live album from Killdozer's final run. Crustacean Records reissues it in 2006.

years.src: Rebel Noise · Mark Prindle · Chicago Reader
years.h: Gerald gets into NYU Law with help from Big Black
years.p: His admission came with a three-page essay about his Killdozer career and a recommendation from [[Santiago Durango|00aa2c29-22a9-4e55-a01b-e51896a379a3]], the ex-[[Big Black|9463868f-edc8-427e-ac07-ea89698e5f15]] guitarist turned lawyer. By 2003 Gerald was a tax lawyer in Los Angeles.
years.xp: He told the Chicago Reader that law school cost him "hundreds of thousands of dollars."

years.cap: Bill and Dan Hobson on stage at Touch and Go's 25th anniversary, Chicago, September 9, 2006
years.h: The original trio plays Touch and Go's 25th as Fuck You, We Reunite!
years.p: Gerald and the Hobsons take the stage at the block party outside the Hideout in Chicago at 3:50 p.m.
years.xp: By then Gerald was a tax lawyer in Los Angeles, Bill Hobson a film grip there, and Dan Hobson a registered nurse still drumming in Madison bands. The same year, the 28-track tribute We Will Bury You came out with a Vig remix of King of Sex.

years.h: Killdozer headlines Madison's Forward Music Festival
years.p: Gerald's one rule for the reunion, from a Chicago Reader interview. The show is at the High Noon Saloon, and Touch and Go sells $35 guaranteed-entry tickets because a $25 festival pass won't get you in if the room fills.
years.xp: Gerald told the Reader that only an insult to someone's dog could break the band up.

years.h: WFMU gets a full live set on Election Night
years.p: The reunited trio plays Brian Turner's show on the night of the 2008 presidential election, during a fall US run.
